span: The circumstantial evidence in order to sustain conviction must be complete and incapable of explanation of any other hypothesis than that of the guilt of the accused
why: Quoted test for when circumstantial evidence can sustain conviction; the court adopts it by applying it in the next paragraph (finding the chain incomplete on the facts).

span: making it impossible to sustain a conviction solely on such circumstantial evidence
why: Court finds the motive/last-seen/recovery circumstances inconclusive and says a conviction cannot be sustained on them alone.

span: as the only safe bases upon which conviction in circumstantial evidence cases can soundly rest
why: Court says the five principles are fundamental rules and the safe basis on which a conviction on circumstantial evidence can rest.

span: failure to examine ballistic expert would be a glaring defect in the prosecution case
why: Reports a precedent about ballistic evidence in a circumstantial case; not about whether circumstantial evidence can sustain conviction.

span: There must be some substantial direct or circumstantial evidence of a call to violence
why: US constitutional case on membership of an organisation; unrelated.

span: Conviction cannot be based solely on circumstantial evidence, unless chain of circumstances is established
why: Headnote holding: conviction on circumstantial evidence needs an established chain, which was missing here, so the accused was acquitted.

span: the circumstantial evidence in order to sustain conviction must be complete and incapable of explanation of any other hypothesis
why: Quoted Shanti Devi principles which the court applies in the next paragraph as 'the above test'; they state when circumstantial evidence can sustain conviction.
